purpose: The village-to-island opening must feel like an RPG investigation, not a single railroaded click path. Counting-house pressure, tavern rumor, harbor work, and optional island clue discovery all need to advance or enrich the main thread.

required_paths.start: Edrin Vale confirms the missing manifest line and frames the investigation as official pressure.
required_paths.expected_state: old_road_farm_path or hidden_landing_harbor_path opens from town pressure into island evidence
required_paths.player_value: The player can begin as a clerk/investigator and still reach island proof.

required_paths.start: Bess Armitage makes the Third Toast a social password before the road opens.
required_paths.expected_state: coded_old_road_path turns tavern speech into island direction
required_paths.player_value: The player can trust rumor culture instead of needing the official route first.

required_paths.start: Mara Pike and Jonah Reed let harbor labor expose the missing line and lantern signal.
required_paths.expected_state: hidden_landing_harbor_path links wharf work to physical cove evidence
required_paths.player_value: The player can follow working-harbor knowledge into the island clue.

required_paths.start: Mara Oren turns the signal rise into an optional clue that changes the journal without blocking progress.
required_paths.player_value: The player who explores gets a richer read of the conspiracy, not just the same quest text.

dialogue_and_objective_effects: Elias Ward changes the route language to the coded old-road marker.
Mara Oren changes the route language to the signal cache and adds a journal enrichment.
Tomas Reed changes the route language to the hidden landing harbor path.
Annelise Crow changes the return/report route choice before the town handoff.
north_star_note: G-18A preserves Newport as a social origin point for a larger pre-Revolutionary island mystery. The player should feel like they are following people, rumors, labor, and geography instead of completing a mechanical checklist.
